title: Import
tokenIntroTitle: Import with a Notion API token
tokenIntroDesc: Create a token in Notion and paste it below. The pages you connect to it can then move to Leafen.

handoff.title: Hand it to an agent
handoff.body: Your agent reads Notion and shows you a plan; once you approve it, Leafen moves it.
handoff.copiedConnect: Copied. Paste it into your agent. It shows here once the agent connects.
handoff.copiedStart: Copied. Paste it into your agent. It makes the Notion connection with you and goes on from there.
handoff.start: Help me move my Notion into my Leafen ({{origin}}), workspace_id {{id}}. In your first answer to this — the one that reports your connection, if you connect first — tell me how the move goes, in these words: “{{firstWords}}” Then, with Leafen’s tools, read the migration guide (leafen_notion_migration_guide), call leafen_notion_migration_sources and follow them.
handoff.firstWords: Here’s how moving your Notion goes: connect Notion → Leafen reads it → I ask you one question, with my recommendations (where it goes, people with no account here, what moves) → Leafen moves it all — content, formats, templates and comments — and checks it against Notion → I report once. All of it happens in this conversation. Some of how things look isn’t in what Notion gives other programs (full width, page layouts, board columns, rows put in order by hand and the like): if I can see your Notion in a browser, I match them; if not, they come in as Leafen’s defaults this time and the report lists each. Nothing moves before you approve, and reading Notion changes nothing there. How long it takes depends on how much there is: Leafen works it out once it has read the structure, in a few minutes, and I’ll tell you then. I need you twice: for the Notion connection, and to answer that one question. In between you can do other things — Leafen tells you in its inbox as each stage ends.
handoff.finish: Finish the Notion import I made myself into my Leafen ({{origin}}), workspace_id {{id}}, migration_id {{migration}}. Read the migration guide (leafen_notion_migration_guide) from section 6, then have Leafen read what formats_left_groups in leafen_notion_migration_status says is left (one by one with list formats_left) from my Notion with leafen_notion_migration_formats.
handoff.sameConversation: Paste it into the same conversation you connected your agent in.
handoff.agentGoesOn: Your agent takes it from here.
handoff.tokenStays: The token is kept in Leafen only and never goes to your agent.

notionSteps.title: In Notion
items: Open app.notion.com/developers/connections (“Developer connections” in Notion’s developer tools) and log in to Notion if it asks.

If the list already has a connection you made for Leafen before, open it instead of making a new one (one you no longer use can be deleted in its page’s “Danger zone”). Otherwise click “New connection”, type a name such as Leafen in “Connection name”, keep “API token” under “Authentication method”, choose the workspace to move if it asks, and click “Create connection”. Creating a connection means agreeing to Notion’s developer terms.
On the connection’s page, open “Content access”, click “Edit access”, choose the top pages to move and click “Save”. Pages under them come along.

Back in “Configuration”, tick “Read content” and “Read comments” under “Capabilities” (without “Read comments” no comments come). Leafen only reads, so “Update content”, “Insert content” and “Insert comments” may stay off. Under “User capabilities”, choose “Read user information including email addresses” (so Notion people match Leafen members by e-mail and can be invited). Then copy the token (ntn_…) with the copy button beside “API token”.
notionSteps.token: Then put the token in the “Notion API token” field below.

issue.view_filter_deleted_property_one: {{count}} view condition names a property deleted in Notion — Notion doesn’t give it to a connection and deleted properties don’t move, so the Leafen view comes without it
issue.view_filter_deleted_property_other: {{count}} view conditions name a property deleted in Notion — Notion doesn’t give them to a connection and deleted properties don’t move, so the Leafen views come without them
issue.view_filters_unread_one: {{count}} database or view couldn’t be read in Notion — whether its conditions name deleted properties can’t be told
issue.view_filters_unread_other: {{count}} databases or views couldn’t be read in Notion — whether their conditions name deleted properties can’t be told
issue.computed_kept_beside_one: {{count}} formula or rollup of rows merged or split into another database computes otherwise than the column of its name there, so it comes in a column of its own beside it, ‘<name> (<its database>)’ — those rows compute as in Notion
issue.computed_kept_beside_other: {{count}} formulas or rollups of rows merged or split into another database compute otherwise than the column of their name there, so they come in a column of their own beside it, ‘<name> (<their database>)’ — those rows compute as in Notion

migration.reconnecting: Can’t reach the server. The import goes on there, and this picks up once it’s back.

readLost.summary: Can’t get the scan’s summary for the plan from the server, so it’s read again every few seconds. Once it comes, “View plan” shows here.
readLost.plan: Can’t get the plan from the server, so it’s read again every few seconds. It shows here once it comes.
readLost.migration: Can’t get how far the move is from the server, so it’s read again every few seconds. It shows here once it comes.
readLost.job: Can’t get the import’s progress from the server, so it’s read again every few seconds. The import goes on there.

migration.stepRerun: Placing and removing the blocks the source moved or deleted…
migration.stepFormats: Matching widths, layouts and views to the source’s screen…
migration.phaseStill: unchanged for {{time}} — it keeps going by itself
migration.phaseMadeLater: Leafen makes it all once reading ends.
migration.phaseChangesLater: Everything from the last finished move ({{time}}) is here; once reading ends, only what changed in Notion changes.
migration.tally: {{made}} made new · {{changed}} changed · {{kept}} left as they were
migration.closeAnytime: You can close this window. The import continues and appears under Completed.
migration.retryGoesOn: Retry goes on from this step, and nothing before it is read from Notion again.

stages.rerun: placing and removing the blocks Notion moved or deleted
stages.formats: matching widths, layouts and views to Notion’s screen
stages.finish: finishing templates and rows’ Notion history

migration.canceledLead: What it made so far doesn’t show in the workspace. Importing again reads Notion again from the start and doesn’t make what it already moved twice.
migration.canceledAgainLead: What earlier runs moved stays in the workspace. Pages and blocks this run already matched to Notion stay as it changed them, and the pages it was making don’t show. Importing again reads Notion again from the start and doesn’t make what it already moved twice.
migration.draftFailed: Couldn’t prepare the import. Try again.
migration.commentsUnavailable: Notion didn’t provide the comments, so they weren’t moved.
migration.commentsUnreadable_one: Notion didn’t provide the comments of {{count}} page or block, so they weren’t moved.
migration.commentsUnreadable_other: Notion didn’t provide the comments of {{count}} pages or blocks, so they weren’t moved.
migration.filesOmitted_one: {{count}} file couldn’t be brought because Notion no longer gives it. Don’t delete the Notion original while it’s missing: restore it in Notion, then copy it again.
migration.filesOmitted_other: {{count}} files couldn’t be brought because Notion no longer gives them. Don’t delete the Notion originals while they’re missing: restore them in Notion, then copy them again.
migration.filesOmittedBesides_one: Besides, {{count}} file earlier runs couldn’t copy is listed in the import report.
migration.filesOmittedBesides_other: Besides, {{count}} files earlier runs couldn’t copy are listed in the import report.
migration.filesOmittedEarlier_one: {{count}} file earlier runs couldn’t copy is listed in the import report.
migration.filesOmittedEarlier_other: {{count}} files earlier runs couldn’t copy are listed in the import report.

failure.provider: Notion rejected or didn’t respond to a request. Try again in a little while.
failure.tokenRejected: Notion no longer accepts the connection’s token. Copy the integration’s token again (or create a new one) and connect it, then try again; what was already moved stays.
failure.connection: The Notion connection can’t be used: the integration was removed or its token changed. Connect it again, then try again.
failure.scope: Notion didn’t let the connection read the pages you chose. Share them with the integration again, then try again.
failure.file: A file stored in Notion couldn’t be copied. Try again; if it keeps failing, leave files out or move them by hand.
failure.planChanged: The plan changed while it ran. Check the plan, then run it again.
failure.planBlocked: The plan can’t be carried out as written. Check it with your agent.
failure.people: Matching Notion’s people to members stopped. Try again from Settings → Import.
failure.create: Leafen couldn’t create the imported content. Try again; what was already moved stays.
failure.leafen: Leafen stopped while importing. Try again; what was already moved stays.
failure.trashed: A page or row it was changing was moved to the trash during the run.
failure.deleted: A page or row it was changing was deleted during the run.

migration.agentWorking: Your agent is on it. You can close this window.
migration.agentRunning: Leafen is moving it on its own. You can close this window and your agent. Your inbox tells you when it’s done; then tell your agent “It’s done,” and it checks the result and reports back.
migration.agentDone: Tell your agent “It’s done,” and it checks the result and reports back.
migration.afterDone: If you keep writing in Notion, Completed › “Import changes again” brings only what’s new or changed. Once everything has moved, make Notion read-only or stop using it — what you write in Leafen doesn’t go back to Notion.
migration.agentPlanningLead: Your agent shows you the plan in your conversation, and Leafen moves it once you approve.
migration.commentsStopped: Comments stopped on the way. Those moved until then stay; the rest are in Notion.
migration.phaseInner: {{read}} of about {{total}} blocks inside them read
migration.phaseTemplates_one: {{count}} template, not counted among the rows
migration.phaseTemplates_other: {{count}} templates, not counted among the rows
